attack_description: GroupKFold(group=material) never separates metallurgically near-identical alloy aliases (e.g. 316/316L/316LN/316Ti, or Hastelloy-C-276/Alloy-C-276/Inco-C-276) since each alias is a distinct string label but the SAME or near-identical chemistry. This re-runs the identical feature engineering, HistGBM model, seed, and metrics with the group axis changed from raw material string to metallurgical FAMILY (ASM Handbook Vol.3; Sedriks 1996; Uhlig-Revie 2008), which guarantees all aliases of one family fall in the same fold.
attacks_claim: corr-rate-qspr-v1/HANDOFF.md headline: leave-material-out (GroupKFold group=material) HistGBM R2=0.316 on log10(corrosion rate mm/yr), described as 'the reproducible artifact of record' for corrosion-rate QSPR in this module.

dataset.name: NIST CORR-DATA (Dow Chemical Co.) derived reference

family_classification.method: ordered keyword/regex substring rules, same methodology as in-tree COMPOSITION lookup; first-match-wins
family_classification.reference: ASM Handbook Vol.3: Stainless Steels; Sedriks 1996 Corrosion of Stainless Steels; Uhlig-Revie 2008 Corrosion and Corrosion Control

refutation_criterion: REFUTED if family_safe.gbm.r2 <= 0.0 OR family_safe_error_reduction_vs_best_baseline_pct <= 0.0 (on the identical classified-subset rows/features/model/seed as material_safe_subset); SURVIVED otherwise, even if reduced relative to material_safe_subset.

material_safe_full_cohort_reference.note: replicates corr-rate-qspr-v1 exactly (full n=7699 cohort, GroupKFold group=material, 5-fold)

scope_honesty: Diagnostic on bare metal/alloy substrate corrosion (NIST CORR-DATA), same scope ceiling as corr-rate-qspr-v1: NOT organic-coating barrier performance. No candidate/coating superiority claim.
